items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: Harry Shields was the brother of the late Larry Shields.

ctx.x: Because Arthur Godfrey had, happened to be in Chicago for a week with his horse, Goldie. He has a horse that does tricks. This horse, his name is Goldie. And he happened to be in Chicago that week, staying at the Edgewater Beach Hotel. Because during the day, he was performing at a stock show. His horse was performing at a stock show. And he got, and Arthur Godfrey doesn't go anywhere without his banjo. And he has a beautiful, expensive banjo. And he flipped over the banjo. We were doing two shows a night in…
You know, Arthur Godfrey had some pretty good musicians with him at the time.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: Larry is his brother who passed away many years ago.

ctx.x: Harry, yeah. Larry is his brother who passed away many years ago. Now Larry, the one that was in California, he wrote clarinet, marmalade, plus many other tunes. Oh. No, I'm talking about having had the pleasure of working with the late Monk Hazel, the late Harry Shields, and the late Almond Hug, and of course the late Sharky's. I feel really honored having had the opportunity of working with guys like that. And of course I really enjoyed working with Al Hurd and Pete Fountain, and of course Bob Havens and all…
I haven't heard him in years.
